rv.q: Fortunately, Theis is also more than capable of delivering an excellent interpretation of this complicated and somewhat awkward play.

Well-cast and imaginatively staged by adapter and director Kevin Theis, Oak Park Theatre Festival’s telling of “The Winter’s Tale” is a consistently engaging and occasionally enthralling way to spend a midsummer evening.
All that is positive, sweet, and redemptive in the play—the openhearted expressions of friendship, the warmhearted comic turns, the full-throttle romance in the second half—works like a charm.

cn.t: This high-spirited production emphasizes the play's redemptive warmth over its darkness, with strong casting and imaginative staging making for an engaging summer evening that resonates with contemporary themes.
